profile.campus: Sunnyvale, California (Equinix SV4, Silicon Valley network)
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's SV4 facility at 255 Caspian Drive in Sunnyvale, California, part of the company's dense Silicon Valley interconnection network anchored by facilities across San Jose, Santa Clara, Palo Alto, and Sunnyvale. Equinix's own published specifications describe SV4 as spanning 67,619 square feet, with N+1 power and cooling redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 2kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including ISO 27001, HIPAA, and SOC 2 Type II. Equinix markets SV4, like its other Silicon Valley buildings, as serving what it calls the largest concentration of high-tech companies and peering hubs in the world, with access to major financial and enterprise networks. Equinix was founded in Silicon Valley in 1998 by former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers Al Avery and Jay Adelson on the premise of providing a neutral place for competing networks to interconnect, and remains headquartered nearby in Redwood City; the company converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Equinix's SV4 page did not disclose a specific opening date for this Sunnyvale facility in the material fetched this session.

Silicon Valley Power, Sunnyvale's municipal utility, has cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in its own capacity planning, a dynamic distinct from newer data center markets given how built-out and power-constrained the Bay Area grid already is after decades of continuous data center development since Equinix's own 1998 founding in the area.

Sunnyvale's Moffett Park and Caspian Drive corridor, where SV4 sits, has grown into one of the denser clusters of colocation and cloud-adjacent facilities in the South Bay, drawing additional operators alongside Equinix as demand for direct, low-latency connections to Silicon Valley's concentration of technology and financial-sector tenants has continued to grow.

reading.body:
Equinix SV4 is a 67,619 square foot retail colocation facility in Sunnyvale with N+1 redundancy for both power and cooling, but its power capacity is not published. Without a megawatt figure, its scale cannot be assessed against other data centers or converted to an equivalent rack or accelerator count. The facility sits within Equinix's 12-facility Silicon Valley metro cluster, which serves over 10,500 customers and constitutes the region's stated largest retail colocation footprint.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities, of which only 11 publish power capacity figures totaling 365 MW. SV4 does not rank in the 11 published facilities and so does not appear in the state's disclosed capacity. Without its megawatt rating, this facility cannot be positioned in the state's power hierarchy or measured against the constraint that binds AI scaling to the grid.

The dual N+1 redundancy tier qualifies SV4 to host mission-critical colocation workloads with fault tolerance. Retail colocation serves many tenants with mixed workloads, not purpose-built AI training or inference clusters. To determine whether this campus matters to AI scaling would require the operator to publish its power capacity and its current or committed allocation to accelerator-dense tenants, neither of which appears on its specification page.
